subtitle: The tournament returns with heavier machinery

body: Twisted Metal is Eat Sleep Play's PlayStation 3 vehicular combat game, first released in North America on 14 February 2012. Cars and other armed vehicles fight through arenas where surviving an attack matters more than completing a clean lap. The release reboots the series around its familiar mixture of violent competition and grotesque personalities. Weapons, routes and the handling of each vehicle shape the next confrontation. A street becomes useful because it offers an escape, a pickup or a way to bring an opponent into range, rather than simply belonging to a racecourse.

The game places considerable emphasis on multiplayer, with split-screen and online modes supporting different scales of competition. Nuke gives teams a multi-stage objective involving an enemy leader, a missile launcher and a target suspended beneath a helicopter. Completing one part does not end the contest; it creates another task that opponents can interrupt. The player must connect driving and weapon use to the current stage of that shared operation. The arena's value changes as the objective moves, giving a team reasons to defend one place and then rapidly shift attention elsewhere.

David Jaffe directed the game, with Scott Campbell producing and contributing to its design. A delay moved the planned 2011 release into early 2012. The multiplayer design supported up to four players locally and sixteen online, bringing the series' chaotic confrontations into a larger console-network setting. Official online play ended in 2019. The release remains a substantial return to Twisted Metal's central idea: a vehicle is a combat character whose movement, size and equipment matter inside an arena that is constantly being reshaped by the people trying to destroy one another.
